text:
**The asset experienced tree-cover loss, but the evidence does not establish permanent deforestation.** In 2021, 81.3 hectares—2.23% of the asset—were identified as lost, and 98% of that event area was mapped as forest in 2020.

Uruguay’s 2021 forest map classifies 68.1 hectares of the loss area as planted pine forest and none as native forest; the remaining 13.2 hectares were outside mapped forest. The loss could therefore include plantation harvesting rather than permanent forest conversion.

An additional 37.3 hectares of loss occurred in patches smaller than 0.5 hectares and was not counted as an event.
